scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: An egg slides around a non-stick pan like it's on ice. If nothing sticks to it, how does the coating stick to the pan?

scenes.name: ptfe
scenes.text: Most non-stick pans use a coating called PTFE, a plastic made of carbon and fluorine.

scenes.name: slippery
scenes.text: Fluorine atoms form a tight shield, so food molecules find almost nothing to grab onto.

scenes.name: bond
scenes.text: To fix it on the pan, the metal is roughened, then primer layers are baked on so the coating locks into the bumps.

scenes.name: heat
scenes.text: Very high heat can damage the coating, so these pans work best on low to medium heat.

scenes.name: scratch
scenes.text: Metal spoons can scratch the coating, so wooden or silicone tools help it last longer.

scenes.name: ceramic
scenes.text: Ceramic non-stick pans use a different, glass-like coating, and cast iron becomes non-stick with seasoning.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Slippery fluorine, rough metal underneath. Follow for more on how things really work.
